title: MD disputes police report of slaying
article: A forensic pathologist has contradicted police testimony,saying a psychologically troubled man fatally shot by three officers was not in close quarters with police.

Citing the absence of gunpowder around the victim's wounds, Dr. Michael Pollanen yesterday told the inquest into the 2004 death of O'Brien Christopher\-Reid, 26, that the shots were not fired from close or intermediate range.

Toronto police Sgt. Darren Berezowski has testified Christopher-Reid was within 1.2 to 1.5 metres of him when he fired his weapon, and that the victim was only a step away from another officer at the time.
Berezowski said Christopher-Reid, holding a knife above his head, had charged toward that officer, John Liggio.
In 2004, the Special Investigations Unit, which cleared the three officers, found they fired a total of eight shots at about the same time.
Pollanen said four shots hit the victim two in the back, one entered from the left side of his chest and one grazed his back from the right.
Lawyer Peter Rosenthal, representing the victim's mother, asked the doctor if any of the gunshots hit the victim from the front.

Members of Toronto's black community have stated that the June 13, 2004, shooting at Edwards Gardens was an unprovoked attack on a black man by police. The victim had been diagnosed with paranoid delusional disorder earlier in 2004.
